scope: Proposition 4.6 (Conditional obstacle moments) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix finitely many separated interval-compatible obstacles with filled isolating neighborhoods Ui as in Proposition 3.7. Let a test disk lie in a pin-free simply connected neighborhood U0, with room for a surrounding buffered cut whose filled interior lies in U0. Require U0 to be disjoint from every Ui. Let Y be a zero-total smearing in the test disk, satisfying (4.1) at its scale. Conditional on all the pins, ∥Y ∥Lp ≤ Cp (p < ∞). (4.11) The constants depend on the macroscopic arrangement, the weight bound, the number of obstacles, and the bound on W-subpath counts, but not on the mesh or the microscopic pin probabilities. No uniformity as obstacle separations vanish is asserted here.
